interest: Shows Allied intelligence on Japanese complicity in Indonesia's independence struggle via covert groups like 'Black Fan' and 'Day Sang Ka'.
overview: Despatch No. 707 (1946) transmits a news report on Japanese soldiers arming and training Indonesian nationalists via covert networks like 'Black Fan', quoting a Japanese police officer's boast of political, if not military, victory.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a Netherlands News Agency press report on clandestine Japanese activities and collaboration with Indonesian nationalists in Java.
subfiles.from: J. Webb Benton, Counselor of Embassy (for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 707: Benton forwards a 1946 article on Japanese covert activity in Java claiming political, though not military, victory.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 707 from The Hague transmitting article entitled 'Japanese Secret Activity'
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: News report detailing Japanese underground operations, weapons distribution, clandestine organizations, and military instruction supporting Indonesian nationalists in Java.
subfiles.summary: Article describes Japanese-run groups 'Black Fan' and 'Day Sang Ka' arming and training Indonesian nationalists after surrender, with Japanese officers serving as military advisers.
subfiles.title: Article 'Japanese Secret Activity' from Anep-Aneta Bulletin
